title: QUIC: Add dissection of MP-QUIC draft-deconinck-quic-multipath
description:
hi,

I have extended the quic dissector with the MP-QUIC frames from the deconnick draft
[https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-deconinck-quic-multipath/].

I am currently working on the implementation of the draft to perform tests on the implementation.

I would be pleased about feedback to the extension

notes.body: use proto_tree_add_bitmask

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1679/diffs?diff_id=136638120&start_sha=1e277792196ca5b6e7882c451aff5c69ea67c0e1#d4fb11677787b1f9a3875d35bb865f4ba9d238ee_2002_2047)
I have adjusted this

Look good, do you have a pcap ?

@IvanNardi can you look too ?
At the beginning of the file there is an "Extension" list where all the Internet-Drafts/RFCs supported are listed: could you add a link to this new draft, with the related version, please?
yes, sure i did it.

This is a correct change but it seems unrelated to the multi-path stuff: could you post it in a separate commit/MR, please? This way, you probably simplify the back-porting process to old releases: this fix is definitely a back-port material, but I don't know about the multi-path support

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1679/diffs?diff_id=136638120&start_sha=1e277792196ca5b6e7882c451aff5c69ea67c0e1#d4fb11677787b1f9a3875d35bb865f4ba9d238ee_585_623)

Is this cast (and all the similar ones below) really necessary? I am asking because the pattern "proto_tree_add_item_ret_varint + offset update" is very common in this dissector and this cast is never present: I think that we need to be consistent, either everywhere or nowhere
I don't know exactly which section you mean, but I have adapted it at this point according to @alagoutte.
Space after "if", to be consistent with the rest of the file

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1679/diffs?diff_id=136638120&start_sha=1e277792196ca5b6e7882c451aff5c69ea67c0e1#d4fb11677787b1f9a3875d35bb865f4ba9d238ee_2028_2077)
The implementation you are working on, is it publicly available?
